en.title: Bible Verses for Depression: 19 Scriptures for Dark Days
en.description: Nineteen Bible verses for depression: lament psalms, godly people at their lowest, God near the crushed, and why seeing a doctor is not a lack of faith.
en.intro: The Bible does not tell a heavy heart to hurry up. It gives sorrow words, in psalms that say "How long?" and a prayer that ends in darkness. The nineteen passages below are in five groups: honest lament, people who hit their limit, God near the crushed, getting help, and hope that returns slowly. Verses can sit beside you on a low day. They are not a treatment. If your low mood lasts weeks or you think about harming yourself, please see a doctor or counselor, and tell a pastor or friend.

groups.heading: Psalms that say how bad it feels
groups.reflection: You are allowed to pray without tidying up your feelings first. These psalms are written prayers, kept in Scripture for exactly such days. David asks "How long?" in Psalm 13 and groans through the night in Psalm 6. Psalm 143 describes a spirit growing faint. Psalm 88, from the sons of Korah, is the bleakest. It still opens by addressing God as the God of my salvation, so even despair is brought to him.

groups.heading: People of faith who reached their limit
groups.reflection: Deep weariness has happened to people God used. In 1 Kings 19, Elijah is exhausted and afraid, and asks to die. God's first response is a nap, food and water, not a lecture. Paul tells the Corinthians in 2 Corinthians 1 that he felt crushed beyond his strength and despaired even of life. In 2 Corinthians 4 he says he was perplexed but not in despair. In Psalm 42 the writer talks to his own soul and tells it to hope.

groups.heading: God is close to the crushed
groups.reflection: These verses say God moves toward people who are low, not away. Psalm 34 says he is near the brokenhearted, and Psalm 147 says he binds up their wounds. Isaiah 42 promises that a bruised reed will not be broken, a picture of someone fragile being handled gently. Psalm 130 is a song for pilgrims, and Psalm 40 recalls being lifted from a pit. The two prayers cry from the depths. They do not claim the climb was quick.

groups.heading: Is it okay to get help? What the Bible shows
groups.reflection: Yes. Seeking medical or pastoral help fits what Scripture shows. Jesus, in Mark 2, uses an everyday line that the sick need a doctor, and he does not object to doctors. Paul advises Timothy in 1 Timothy 5 to take something for his stomach and frequent ailments. Galatians 6 tells believers to carry one another's burdens. Proverbs 12 notes that a kind word lifts a weighed-down heart. Depression is often more than a spiritual problem, so a doctor, counselor and church can work together.

groups.heading: Hope that comes back slowly
groups.reflection: Hope in these verses usually returns in stages, not all at once. In Psalm 71, the writer says God will revive him again after many troubles, so recovery is something he expects but has not yet seen. Paul's prayer in Romans 15 asks God to fill the church in Rome with hope by the Holy Spirit. It is a prayer for you, not something to manufacture. On a bad day, borrowing someone else's hope is enough.

faq.q: What does the Bible say about depression?
faq.a: The Bible never uses the word, but it describes deep sorrow often. Psalm 13, Psalm 88 and 1 Kings 19:3-8 show believers in despair, and God meeting them. Psalm 34:18 says he is near the brokenhearted.

faq.q: Is depression a sin or a lack of faith?
faq.a: Nothing on this page says so. Elijah, Paul and the psalm writers all had low seasons and were not rejected by God. Depression is a health condition as well as a spiritual struggle, and treatment is appropriate.

faq.q: Should a Christian see a doctor or counselor for depression?
faq.a: Yes. Mark 2:17 uses doctors as a normal image, and 1 Timothy 5:23 shows Paul advising a remedy for Timothy's ailments. Seeing a doctor, counselor or pastor is wise and does not replace prayer.

faq.q: What is a good Bible verse when you feel hopeless?
faq.a: Psalm 34:18 is short and honest. Psalm 130:1-2 is a prayer to say from the depths, and Romans 15:13 asks God to fill you with hope. Choose one and repeat it, even if you do not feel it yet.
